insight.title: Why a Period Feels Like a Threat
insight.subtitle: How the internet turned basic grammar into a passive-aggressive weapon.
insight.notificationHook: Why a single period feels so hostile.

sections.text: Receiving a text that ends in a period used to mean a sentence was finished. Now, it feels like an active threat, signaling unspoken anger, coldness, or a total conversational shutdown.
In digital spaces, we communicate tone through absence. Because we usually send messages without punctuation, adding a formal period feels deliberate—a silent, sharp exclamation point of disapproval.
We’ve built an entire unwritten syntax of emotional safety. "lol" is no longer a laugh; it’s a shield. Lowercase is intimate. Proper grammar is reserved for enemies and bosses.
We didn't kill the period; we just weaponized it.
